LanguageContext.jsx i18n

Cross-cutting i18n layer. Loads all locale files at build time, exposes a t(key, vars) translation function, and persists the user's language choice to localStorage. Independent of the hexagonal adapter system — but anchored to it at one point: IInstitution.defaultLocale sets the language the app opens with.

Parent
context/
Hook
const { t, locale, setLocale, locales } = useLanguage()
Locale files
src/locales/ — ar, en, es, fr, hi, ja, zh (eager Vite glob)
Storage key
{storagePrefix}-locale in localStorage
Adapter touchpoint
IInstitution.defaultLocale — the locale to open with if no saved preference

How translation works

All 7 locale files are loaded eagerly at build time via import.meta.glob("../locales/*.js", { eager: true }). Each file exports { meta, strings, default } where strings is a flat key-value map.

The t(key, vars) function resolves a key against the active locale, falls back to English if the key is missing, and then falls back to the raw key string if English also doesn't have it. Named interpolation uses {variableName} placeholders:

// inside any component
import { useLanguage } from "../context/LanguageContext.jsx";

function MyComponent() {
  const { t } = useLanguage();

  return (
    <div>
      {t("bank.title")}                       // → "COURSE BANK" (en) or "课程库" (zh)
      {t("sem.sh.total", { count: 128 })}     // → "128 SH total"
      {t("header.credits.placed", { n: 64 })} // → "64 SH placed"
    </div>
  );
}

What useLanguage() returns

t
function
t(key: string, vars?: Record<string, string|number>) → string. Translate a key. Falls back to English, then to the raw key. Performs {name} interpolation.
locale
string
Current locale code, e.g. "en", "zh", "ar".
setLocale
function
setLocale(code: string) → void. Switch to a different locale. Persists to localStorage. React re-renders all components that call useLanguage().
locales
array
Array of all available locale metadata objects: { code, name, nativeName, dir }. Sorted: English first, then alphabetical by nativeName. Used by Header to populate the language picker.

Locale file format

Each file in src/locales/ must export:

// src/locales/en.js (example)
export const meta = {
  code:       "en",
  name:       "English",
  nativeName: "English",
  dir:        "ltr",
};

export const strings = {
  "bank.title":            "COURSE BANK",
  "bank.search.placeholder": "Search courses…",
  "sem.sh.total":          "{count} SH total",
  // …
};

export default strings;

Institution adapter touchpoint

LanguageContext reads one field from the IInstitution adapter: institution.defaultLocale. This determines the language the app opens with on first visit (before the user has made a choice). If the field is absent or null, "en" is used.

// src/adapters/northeastern/institution.js
export default {
  id:            "northeastern",
  defaultLocale: "en",  // <-- what LanguageContext reads
  // …
};
✦
Adding a new language: Create src/locales/xx.js following the format above. LanguageContext picks it up automatically via the Vite glob — no code changes needed. The language picker in Header will show the new option immediately.

What's not translated

LanguageContext translates UI chrome — labels, buttons, placeholders, aria text. It does not translate course titles, descriptions, or requirement names, which come from the course catalog and major requirement JSONs.
